CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. James is a 42-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain sustained 5 days ago during a skiing accident. She was skiing on double black diamonds when she lost control and fell, jamming her right index finger on an unknown object during the fall. She denies other injuries from the incident. Pain is rated 7 out of 10. She has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. She denies having applied ice or splinting to the finger.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports chronic constipation, otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation
Appendectomy at age 7

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skier

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand x-ray reviewed: Normal anatomy with no fractures. All joints and bones in appropriate positions. Physical examination of right index finger reveals tenderness to palpation, pain with traction, and pain with compression over the distal interphalangeal joint.

RESULTS
X-ray right hand: No fractures, normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right index finger distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint sprain. Placed right index finger splint. Prescribed Mobic 15 mg once daily for 14 days as strong anti-inflammatory. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing. Hand therapy to be considered at follow-up visit if needed.
